title: Microsoft Teams: QR code images from external senders are blurred by default
summary: The QR code behaviour, default, rollout dates and Teams licensing are supported. The external-domain guidance incorrectly implies that every custom policy bypasses organisation settings, although custom policies can inherit them. The statement that administrators cannot tune obscuring also goes beyond the documented absence of enable and disable controls.

claims.where: controls[0].ui and controls[0].api; summary; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No admin UI or API for enabling or disabling QR code obscuring is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams QR code obscuring admin controls PowerShell Graph allow list tuning detection licensing license pricing; Teams QR code detection processing allowlist configure PowerShell Graph. Read the feature page and Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration; no switch found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: A tenant cannot tune QR code obscuring.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams QR code obscuring detection algorithm image data processing tuning; Teams QR code detection processing allowlist configure PowerShell Graph. Read the feature page: no enable/disable controls stated, but no statement that tuning is impossible.
claims.fix: Remove 'or tune it' from the sentence 'Learn states that there are no admin controls to enable or disable the behaviour, so a tenant cannot switch it off or tune it.' The cited Learn page states only that no admin enable/disable controls exist.

claims.claim: Users assigned a custom external access policy communicate with its domains, not organisation settings.
